answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a costly, time-built reputation instead of free accounts: each agent must lock a small refundable stake and earn trust only through verified, useful work over weeks. Faking thousands of identities then costs real stake and time, while one honest agent slowly gains weight, like sediment hardening into shale. A shared harbor of audited work history lets peers check that record before trusting a newcomer, and a sudden comet of new accounts arriving together triggers throttling and review rather than instant rewards.
